title: Rationalization
competency: Rationalize denominators that contain a single radical or a sum or difference with radicals.

keywords.def: Rewriting a fraction so its denominator has no radicals.
The expression you multiply the top and bottom by to rationalize a denominator, for example √3/√3.
The same two terms with the opposite sign between them: √a + √b and √a − √b are conjugates.

en.text: A fraction like 1/√3 has an irrational denominator. To fix it, multiply by a rationalizing factor equal to 1, such as √3/√3. The value does not change. The denominator becomes √3 × √3 = 3, a rational number.

am.text: እንደ 1/√3 ያለ ክፍልፋይ ኢ-ምክንያታዊ ተከፋይ አለው። ለማስተካከል ከ1 ጋር እኩል በሆነ አባዥ አባዛ፤ ለምሳሌ √3/√3። እሴቱ አይለወጥም። ተከፋዩ √3 × √3 = 3 ይሆናል፤ ይህም ምክንያታዊ ቁጥር ነው።

screens.title: Which is easier?
screens.text: √3 ≈ 1.732. You need the value of 1/√3 without a calculator.
screens.ask: Which is easier to work out by hand: 1 ÷ 1.732, or 1.732 ÷ 3?
screens.after: Dividing by 3 is much easier. And 1/√3 = √3/3, so both give about 0.577. Read on.

screens.title: Rationalization
paras: A fraction such as 1/√3 has an irrational denominator. This makes it hard to work with.
Rationalizing the denominator means rewriting it with a rational denominator.
We multiply by a rationalizing factor that equals 1, such as √3/√3.
Multiplying by 1 does not change the value. For 1/√a, the factor is √a/√a.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Rewriting a fraction so its denominator has no radicals.
What you multiply the top and bottom by, for example √3/√3. It equals 1.

screens.title: Pick the factor
screens.text: Which rationalizing factor do you use for 2/√3?
screens.why: √3 × √3 = 3, which is rational. The factor equals 1, so the value stays the same.
screens.clue: Which radical is in the denominator? Multiply by that over itself.

screens.text: Multiply top and bottom by the rationalizing factor.
steps: (c) For a cube root, aim for a perfect cube: 1/∛2 × ∛4/∛4 = ∛4/∛8

screens.title: True or false?
screens.why: √3/√3 = 1, and multiplying by 1 never changes a value.

en.text: When the denominator is a sum or difference like √a − √b, multiply top and bottom by the conjugate, √a + √b. This uses the difference of two squares: (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y². The square roots disappear from the denominator.

am.text: ተከፋዩ እንደ √a − √b ያለ ድምር ወይም ልዩነት ሲሆን ላይና ታችን በተጓዳኙ √a + √b አባዛ። ይህ የሁለት ካሬዎች ልዩነትን ይጠቀማል፤ (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y²። ካሬ ሥሮቹ ከተከፋዩ ይጠፋሉ።

screens.title: Where do the roots go?
screens.text: Asks for products like this one.
screens.after: It is 5 − 3 = 2. The square roots disappear! Read on to see why.

screens.title: Activity 1.25
paras: Each answer has no radicals left.

screens.title: The difference of two squares
paras: This is the difference of two squares: (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y².
Multiplying by the "conjugate" removes the square roots.
Table 1.3 lists the factor to use for each kind of denominator.

screens.title: Name it
defs: The same two terms with the opposite sign between them. √a + √b and √a − √b are conjugates.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.text: What do you multiply 5/(3 + √2) by to rationalize it?

screens.title: (a) and (b)
screens.text: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator.

screens.title: (c): three terms
screens.text: Sometimes one multiplication is not enough.
steps: Start with 1/(√3 − √2 + 1). Multiply top and bottom by (√3 − √2 − 1).
The denominator still has a radical. So multiply again by (2 + √6).

screens.title: Roots disappear
screens.text: Use the difference of two squares.

screens.title: A garden bed
screens.text: A school garden bed in Bahir Dar has area 1 m². Its length is (√2 + 1) m.
screens.ask: Its width is 1/(√2 + 1) m. Rationalize the width.
screens.why: Multiply by (√2 − 1)/(√2 − 1). The denominator is 2 − 1 = 1, so the width is √2 − 1.
screens.clue: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of √2 + 1.
screens.worked: The conjugate of √2 + 1 is √2 − 1. Top: 1 × (√2 − 1) = √2 − 1. Bottom: (√2 + 1)(√2 − 1) = 2 − 1 = 1. So the width is (√2 − 1) m, about 0.414 m.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.why: Table 1.3 uses the conjugate, (√a − √b)/(√a − √b). The same sign leaves a radical.
screens.clue: Look at the last row of Table 1.3. Which sign is in the factor?

items.clue: Square the first term, square the second, then subtract.
Multiply by (√3 + 1)/(√3 + 1). Expand the top carefully.
The new denominator is negative. Watch the signs.

items.why: Multiply by (√2 + √3 − 1) to get 2(√2 + √3 − 1)/(4 + 2√6). Then multiply by (4 − 2√6).
items.clue: Like Example 2(c): you need two steps.
items.worked: Step 1: multiply by (√2 + √3 − 1). The bottom is (√2 + √3)² − 1 = 4 + 2√6. Step 2: multiply by (4 − 2√6). The bottom becomes 16 − 24 = −8. The result is (2 + √2 − √6)/2.

test.text: (a + √b)(a − √b) = a² − b, so it has no radicals left.
test.why: This is the difference of two squares: a² − (√b)² = a² − b.

notes.text: In Example 1(a) the printed book first writes the rationalizing factor as √2/√5, then uses √3/√3. The correct factor is √3/√3.
